headline: Former info advisor Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury taken to DB for questioning
summary: The former chairman of DBC News and advisor to the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was taken from his office in Mohakhali.
details: Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury, former information advisor to the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and former chairman of DBC News, has been taken to the Detective Branch (DB) office.
He was taken from the DBC office in Mohakhali, Dhaka, around 3:30 PM on Wednesday.
DB Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam confirmed the action, stating that an 'unwanted situation' had developed at the office after Chowdhury arrived.
According to the police, he was brought to the DB office to avoid further escalation of the situation at the site.
Two other individuals were also taken to the DB office along with him for questioning.
The police are currently speaking with the individuals to gather more information.
caption:

DB Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam confirmed the action, stating that an 'unwanted situation' had developed at the office after Chowdhury arrived.

Two other individuals were also taken to the DB office along with him for questioning.

headline_marked: [[New garment wages to take effect from Dec]], board agrees
headline: New garment wages to take effect from Dec, board agrees
summary: Worker and employer representatives have agreed to finalize the new minimum wage structure by December, with revised salaries paid in January.
details: The minimum wage board for the garment sector has announced that the new wage structure will come into effect from December 1. This agreement was reached during the board's first meeting on Wednesday in Dhaka.
Worker representative Babul Akhter stated that both sides agreed to the timeline so that workers receive their revised salaries along with their January pay.
The process of determining the new minimum wage was initiated amid significant labor unrest and discontent within the garment industry.
Employers' representative ABM Shamsuddin confirmed that discussions were held in a cordial atmosphere and both parties are committed to completing the process within December.
Wage board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani noted that the board was appointed on November 1 and held its first meeting three days later to discuss legal procedures and methods for determining wages.
Babul Akhter urged protesting workers to remain patient, assuring them that the board is working on their behalf to meet their demands.
caption:
Garment workers will see their new wages take effect from December, with revised pay arriving in January.

The minimum wage board for the garment sector has announced that the new wage structure will come into effect from December 1. This agreement was reached during the board's first meeting on Wednesday in Dhaka.

Worker representative Babul Akhter stated that both sides agreed to the timeline so that workers receive their revised salaries along with their January pay.

The process of determining the new minimum wage was initiated amid significant labor unrest and discontent within the garment industry.

Employers' representative ABM Shamsuddin confirmed that discussions were held in a cordial atmosphere and both parties are committed to completing the process within December.

Wage board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani noted that the board was appointed on November 1 and held its first meeting three days later to discuss legal procedures and methods for determining wages.

Babul Akhter urged protesting workers to remain patient, assuring them that the board is working on their behalf to meet their demands.
